title: A weekly money check-in
description: Five minutes once a week keeps small money surprises from becoming big ones.

body.heading: What to look at
paragraphs: Once a week, check three things: your balance, what bills are due before next payday, and whether your spending this week roughly matched your plan. That is the whole check-in.
Catching a forgotten subscription, a double charge, or a bill due tomorrow takes minutes now — and saves stress, fees, and awkward surprises later.

body.heading: Make it pleasant
paragraphs: Pair the check-in with something nice: a favourite drink, music, a walk afterwards. A routine that feels like care, not homework, is one you will keep.
If you share money with family or a partner, a short, calm weekly chat about upcoming costs prevents most money arguments, which are usually about surprises, not amounts.

body.heading: End with one action
paragraphs: Finish each check-in with at most one action: move a little to savings, cancel one unused thing, set a reminder. One action a week is 52 improvements a year.

takeaway: Five minutes weekly: check your balance, upcoming bills, and pick one small action.
